questions.stem: On which cloud platforms is the Snowflake Marketplace available?

options.text: AWS only
AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure (except Azure Government, which is planned)
Only on-premises Snowflake deployments
Google Cloud and Azure only

explanation.correct: The Snowflake Marketplace is available globally to all accounts on AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, with the exception of Microsoft Azure Government (support planned).

distractors.A: It is not AWS-only; it spans AWS, GCP, and Azure.
distractors.C: Snowflake is a cloud service; there are no on-premises deployments.
distractors.D: AWS is included; the exclusion is only Azure Government.

questions.stem: What is the primary benefit for a provider using Marketplace listings versus maintaining individual sharing relationships?

options.text: Gain write access to all consumer accounts
Automatically copy data into every consumer's storage
Share curated data offerings with many consumers simultaneously
Eliminate the need for consumers to have Snowflake accounts

explanation.correct: Marketplace listings let a provider share curated data offerings with many consumers simultaneously, rather than maintaining sharing relationships with each individual consumer.

distractors.A: Providers do not gain write access to consumer accounts.
distractors.B: Marketplace sharing does not copy data into consumer storage.
distractors.D: Consumers still need Snowflake accounts to access Marketplace listings.

questions.stem: What is the Internal Marketplace in Snowflake?

options.text: A public marketplace for any Snowflake account
A billing dashboard for Marketplace purchases
A replication target for disaster recovery
A curated, secure space for data sharing exclusively within your organization

explanation.correct: The Internal Marketplace is a curated, secure space for collaborative data sharing within your organization; it is similar to the public Marketplace but exclusive to your organization.

distractors.A: The Internal Marketplace is organization-only, not public.
distractors.B: It is a discovery space for internal data products, not a billing dashboard.
distractors.C: It is not a replication target.

questions.stem: Which THREE statements about organizational listings and the Internal Marketplace are correct? (Select THREE)

options.text: They are visible to any account on the public Snowflake Marketplace
They require a reader account to consume
They let you share data products securely within your organization
Providers create and manage them using Provider Studio or the API
Access can be managed by account targeting and RBAC
They can only be created with SnowSQL

explanation.correct: Organizational listings share data products securely within your organization, are created/managed via Provider Studio or the API, and access is managed by account targeting and RBAC.

distractors.A: They are internal-only, not visible on the public Marketplace.
distractors.B: They do not require a reader account.
distractors.F: They are created via Provider Studio or the API, not only SnowSQL.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Cross-Cloud Auto-Fulfillment are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It is available on trial accounts
It requires the consumer to manually copy the data
It automatically replicates your data product to other Snowflake regions without manual replication
A data product is any share or application package attached to your listing
It only works within a single region

explanation.correct: Auto-fulfillment automatically replicates your data product (any share or application package attached to your listing) to other Snowflake regions without manual replication.

distractors.A: Auto-fulfillment is not available on trial accounts; you must use a full account to offer listings.
distractors.B: It removes the need for manual copying, not requires it.
distractors.E: Its purpose is cross-region/cross-cloud fulfillment, not single-region only.

questions.scenario: A provider enables Cross-Cloud Auto-Fulfillment and wonders where the data product lands in a remote region.
questions.stem: What managed construct does Snowflake provision in the remote region?

options.text: A reader account owned by the consumer
A failover group
A secure share area (SSA) managed by Snowflake
A resource monitor

explanation.correct: When you set up Cross-Cloud Auto-Fulfillment, Snowflake manages provisioning for a secure share area (SSA) and the auto-fulfillment of your data product to remote regions.

distractors.A: A reader account is unrelated to auto-fulfillment provisioning and is provider-owned when used.
distractors.B: A failover group is a replication/DR construct, not the auto-fulfillment target.
distractors.D: A resource monitor governs credits, not data-product fulfillment.

questions.scenario: A provider shares a listing privately with a specific consumer account located in a different region than the provider.
questions.stem: A provider shares a listing privately with a consumer in a different region. Which TWO statements about private-listing auto-fulfillment are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Private listings cannot be shared across regions
The consumer must configure replication themselves
Snowsight automatically detects the different region and enables auto-fulfillment
You cannot manually replicate private listings to other regions
Private cross-region listings require a reader account

explanation.correct: For listings shared with specific consumer accounts, Snowsight automatically detects a different region and enables auto-fulfillment, and you cannot manually replicate private listings to other regions.

distractors.A: Private listings can be shared across regions via auto-fulfillment.
distractors.B: The consumer does not configure replication; auto-fulfillment handles it.
distractors.E: A reader account is not required for private cross-region listings.

questions.scenario: A provider configures the auto-fulfillment refresh type for a share so selected objects are available on-demand.
questions.stem: Which setting provides on-demand availability of selected objects?

options.text: FULL_DATABASE
SUB_DATABASE
SUB_DATABASE_WITH_REFERENCE_USAGE
REFERENCE_ONLY

explanation.correct: SUB_DATABASE allows selected objects to be available on-demand. SUB_DATABASE_WITH_REFERENCE_USAGE provides account-level scheduling for application packages.

distractors.A: Specifying FULL_DATABASE for the auto-fulfillment refresh type is deprecated.
distractors.C: SUB_DATABASE_WITH_REFERENCE_USAGE is for account-level scheduling of application packages, not on-demand selected objects.
distractors.D: REFERENCE_ONLY is not a valid auto-fulfillment refresh type.

questions.stem: Which THREE are things a consumer can do on the Snowflake Marketplace? (Select THREE)

options.text: Modify the provider's source data directly
Force the provider to lower their price
Discover and test third-party data sources
Combine new datasets with their existing Snowflake data for new insights
Have datasets available instantly and updated continually
Access the provider's account credentials

explanation.correct: Consumers can discover and test third-party data sources, combine new datasets with their existing Snowflake data for insights, and have datasets available instantly and continually updated.

distractors.A: Consumers cannot modify a provider's source data; shared data is read-only.

questions.scenario: A provider uses the same database across multiple listings and auto-fulfills to a new region.
questions.stem: How many times is that database auto-fulfilled to the new region?

options.text: Once (multiple listings can use the same database, auto-fulfilled once per new region)
Once per listing that uses it
Once per consumer account
It cannot be shared across multiple listings

explanation.correct: Multiple listings can use the same database, but the database is only auto-fulfilled once to a new region.

distractors.B: It is fulfilled once to the region regardless of how many listings use it.
distractors.C: It is not fulfilled per consumer account.
distractors.D: A database can back multiple listings.

questions.scenario: A provider on a trial account tries to publish a listing on the Snowflake Marketplace.
questions.stem: Can they offer the listing?

options.text: Yes; trial accounts can offer any listing
Yes, but only free listings
No; to offer listings you must use a full account (trial accounts cannot)
Yes, but only organizational listings

explanation.correct: Auto-fulfillment is configured on listings, and to offer listings you must use a full account; auto-fulfillment isn't available on trial accounts.

distractors.B: Trial accounts cannot offer listings, free or otherwise.
distractors.D: Trial accounts cannot offer listings, including organizational ones for external fulfillment.

questions.scenario: A provider must become approved to publish public listings and reviews the profile approval timeline.
questions.stem: Approximately how long does Snowflake take to review a provider profile submission?

options.text: About 14 business days
About 1 business day
About 30 business days
Instantly, with no review

explanation.correct: Snowflake reviews your provider profile and responds within approximately 1 business day. If rejected for a policy violation, you receive instructions to correct and resubmit.

distractors.A: 14 days is closer to the maximum for a rejected Native App listing review, not profile approval.
distractors.C: 30 days is not the documented profile review time.
distractors.D: Provider profiles are reviewed, not approved instantly.

questions.scenario: A provider follows the data/share listing approval flow on the Snowflake Marketplace.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about the data/share listing approval flow are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Approved listings are automatically deleted after 24 hours
Snowflake reviews the listing metadata and responds within about 1 business day
If manual publishing was selected, the listing stays approved until you manually publish it
Listings never require Snowflake review
A rejected listing cannot be revised or resubmitted

explanation.correct: Snowflake reviews data/share listing metadata within about 1 business day. If you used manual publishing, the listing remains approved until you manually publish it.

distractors.A: Approved listings are not auto-deleted after 24 hours.
distractors.E: A rejected listing can be revised based on feedback and resubmitted.

questions.scenario: A provider profile has been created but no public listing has been published yet.
questions.stem: What is true about the provider profile's visibility?

options.text: The provider profile is always public immediately after creation
Provider profiles are never visible to consumers
Provider profiles are only visible in the Internal Marketplace
The provider profile won't be visible on the Snowflake Marketplace until a public listing is published

explanation.correct: Provider profiles won't be visible on the Snowflake Marketplace until a public listing is published.

distractors.A: The profile is not public until a public listing is published.
distractors.B: Provider profiles do become visible once a public listing is published.
distractors.C: This visibility rule concerns the public Marketplace, not the Internal Marketplace.

questions.scenario: A provider in a government region configures organizational listings for consumers in commercial or VPS accounts.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about Internal Marketplace listings in government regions are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Consumers can search the Internal Marketplace in Snowsight for government-region listings
Consumers in government regions can access listings programmatically using the Uniform Listing Locator (ULL) or by mounting the shared database
Custom organization profiles are fully supported
Cross-Cloud Auto-Fulfillment can be configured, triggering after the consumer accesses the listing
The ACCESS_HISTORY view for these listings is visible to consumers

explanation.correct: Consumers in government regions can access listings programmatically via the ULL or by mounting the shared database, and Cross-Cloud Auto-Fulfillment can be configured (triggered after the consumer accesses the listing).

distractors.A: Consumers can't search the Internal Marketplace in Snowsight for government-region listings; they use the listing URL.
distractors.C: Custom organization profiles aren't supported in this scenario.
distractors.E: The ACCESS_HISTORY view for these listings isn't visible to consumers.

questions.scenario: A provider offers a paid listing that must reach consumers in a different region.
questions.stem: How must the data product be made available in the other region for a paid listing?

options.text: By manually replicating the data only
By emailing the data to the consumer
Using auto-fulfillment
Paid listings cannot cross regions

explanation.correct: For paid listings, you use auto-fulfillment to make the data product available in other regions. (Free or limited-trial Marketplace listings can use auto-fulfillment or manual replication.)

distractors.A: Manual replication is an option for free/limited-trial listings, but paid listings use auto-fulfillment.
distractors.B: Data is not emailed; sharing uses Snowflake's mechanisms.
distractors.D: Paid listings can cross regions via auto-fulfillment.

questions.scenario: A provider on Business Critical Edition (BCE) uses auto-fulfillment and compares it to VPS deployments.
questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes SSA handling for BCE versus VPS?

options.text: Both BCE and VPS never use an SSA
BCE does not require a separate SSA per region but enforces strict security (e.g., Tri-Secret Secure); VPS and government deployments have a separate SSA per deployment
BCE requires a separate SSA per consumer while VPS shares one SSA globally
VPS does not support auto-fulfillment at all

explanation.correct: For BCE, auto-fulfillment does not require creating a separate SSA for the region but enforces strict security/compliance (e.g., Tri-Secret Secure). VPS and government deployments have a separate SSA for each deployment.

distractors.A: SSAs are used; the difference is in how they are handled per deployment.
distractors.C: BCE does not require a separate SSA per consumer.
distractors.D: VPS supports auto-fulfillment with a separate SSA per deployment.

questions.scenario: A provider plans exactly when auto-fulfillment transfers a data product to a remote region for different listing visibilities.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements about auto-fulfillment timing are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Private listings are auto-fulfilled after the specified consumers get the listing
Public Marketplace listings are auto-fulfilled after a consumer in that region gets the listing
All listings are fully replicated to every region in advance
Auto-fulfillment happens only during a monthly maintenance window
Auto-fulfillment never incurs additional cost

explanation.correct: Private listings are auto-fulfilled after the specified consumers get the listing; public Marketplace listings are auto-fulfilled after a consumer in the specific region gets the listing.

distractors.C: Data products are fulfilled to a region as needed, not pre-replicated to every region.
distractors.D: There is no monthly-window restriction on auto-fulfillment timing.
distractors.E: Making a data product available in other regions incurs additional costs.

questions.scenario: A data platform team wants internal teams to discover trusted, vetted datasets without browsing externally-shared Marketplace listings.
questions.stem: Which capability meets this need?

options.text: Public paid listings on the Snowflake Marketplace
Reader accounts
Cross-region failover groups
Organizational listings in the Internal Marketplace

explanation.correct: Organizational listings in the Internal Marketplace let internal teams discover and access vetted, internal-only data products without browsing externally-shared listings.

distractors.A: Public paid listings are external, not internal-only discovery.
distractors.B: Reader accounts are for non-Snowflake consumers, not internal discovery.
distractors.C: Failover groups are for disaster recovery, not internal data discovery.

questions.scenario: A provider reviews limitations of Snowflake Marketplace V2 listings in VPS deployments (preview).
questions.stem: Which TWO limitations apply to VPS Marketplace customers? (Select TWO)

options.text: VPS providers can create unlimited monetized listings
VPS providers can't create monetized listings
VPS customers can only consume app listings for allowlisted connector listings
VPS customers can consume any app listing without restriction
VPS deployments cannot use auto-fulfillment at all

explanation.correct: For V2 listings in VPS deployments (preview): VPS providers can't create monetized listings, and VPS customers can only consume app listings for allowlisted connector listings.

distractors.A: VPS providers cannot create monetized listings.
distractors.D: VPS customers are restricted to allowlisted connector app listings.
distractors.E: VPS deployments do use auto-fulfillment, with a separate SSA per deployment.
